newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt seen privatising more firms shortly.
newsitem.headline: Egypt seen privatising more firms shortly.

text.p: An Egyptian privatisation official said in remarks published on Sunday the state would sell its majority stake in two partly private firms and offer shares in a handful of others in coming weeks.

Mokhtar Khattab, ministerial adviser at the ministry of public enterprise, told the official al-Ahram daily the state would offer through the stock exchange shares in Shams Housing and Development and Kabo/Nasr Clothing and Textiles so that they come under private control.

He said it would also try and sell by auction or public offerings majority stakes in agriculture and contracting firms which other privatisation officials had said they would sell earlier in the year.
Khattab's remarks come as part of a drive by the public enterprise ministry to speed up privatisation as part of Egypt's economic reforms.
Khattab said other firms from which the state plans to withdraw its controlling interest by June include the listed Extracted Oils and Derivatives and Alexandria Spinning and Weaving/Spinalex.

Last week, Public Enterprise Minister Atef Obeid told a conference that the government would also hasten privatisation in sectors such as banks and heavy industry, days after the state offered to the public shares in sugar, steel and aluminium firms.
